Validate projected range shifts against resurveys (hindcasting)

Source: R/range-shift-validate.R
range_shift_validate.Rd

A range-shift model earns trust when it predicts shifts that have already happened. range_shift_validate() compares the shifts observed between a historical survey and a resurvey (range_shift_resurvey()) with the shifts a model predicted for the same species and period, run from the climate of the first survey to that of the second (hindcasting).

For each measure (lower edge, upper edge, midpoint, optimum) it reports:

  • bias: mean of predicted minus observed shift (m);

  • mae, rmse: mean absolute and root mean square error (m);

  • r, rho: Pearson and Spearman correlation across species;

  • slope: calibration slope of observed on predicted (1 is ideal; below 1, the model overstates differences between species);

  • direction: share of species whose shift has the predicted sign;

  • tracking: mean observed shift divided by mean predicted shift, the share of the expected shift that species realised (1 = full tracking; below 1, a lag), with a bootstrap interval resampling species.

range_shift_expected() gives the simplest prediction, the isotherm shift \(\Delta T / \gamma\) for warming \(\Delta T\) and lapse rate \(\gamma\) (Colwell et al. 2008; Freeman and Freeman 2014). It is the baseline any model must beat.

Usage

range_shift_validate(
  observed,
  predicted,
  drop_truncated = TRUE,
  nboot = 999,
  conf = 0.95,
  seed = NULL
)

range_shift_expected(warming, lapse_rate)

Arguments

observed

Result of range_shift_resurvey(), or a data frame with species and observed shift_* columns.

predicted

Data frame with species and predicted shifts, in columns named like those of observed (shift_lower, shift_upper, shift_midpoint, shift_optimum), or a single column shift used for every measure.

drop_truncated

Leave out edges truncated at the ends of the sampled gradient (needs the truncated_* columns of observed).

nboot

Bootstrap resamples for the tracking interval.

conf

Confidence level.

seed

Optional random seed.

warming

Warming in degrees C between the surveys (or scenarios).

lapse_rate

Temperature lapse rate in degrees C per km.

Value

range_shift_validate(): a tibble with one row per measure.

range_shift_expected(): the expected upslope shift in metres.

References

Colwell, R. K., Brehm, G., Cardelús, C. L., Gilman, A. C. and Longino, J. T. (2008). Global warming, elevational range shifts, and lowland biotic attrition in the wet tropics. Science, 322, 258-261.

Freeman, B. G. and Class Freeman, A. M. (2014). Rapid upslope shifts in New Guinean birds illustrate strong distributional responses of tropical montane species to global warming. PNAS, 111, 4490-4494.

Examples

# Virtual resurvey: species realise 60% of a 200 m expected shift
before <- png_frogs
after <- png_frogs
after$elevation <- after$elevation + 120
obs <- range_shift_resurvey(before, after, gradient = elevation, abundance = abundance)
pred <- data.frame(species = obs$species, shift = range_shift_expected(1, 5))
range_shift_validate(obs, pred, nboot = 199, seed = 1)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 14
#>   measure     n observed predicted  bias   mae  rmse     r   rho slope direction
#>   <chr>   <int>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 lower      42      120       200    80    80    80    NA    NA    NA         1
#> 2 upper      53      120       200    80    80    80    NA    NA    NA         1
#> 3 midpoi…    55      120       200    80    80    80    NA    NA    NA         1
#> 4 optimum    55      120       200    80    80    80    NA    NA    NA         1
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: tracking <dbl>, tracking_lower <dbl>,
#> #   tracking_upper <dbl>
